problem.title: Name the Counter Ratio
problem.statement: A tray contains 6 red counters and 4 blue counters. What is the red-to-blue ratio in simplest form?
hints: Keep red first and divide both counts by the same common factor.

solutionSteps.title: Preserve order and simplify
solutionSteps.body: Red-to-blue is 6:4. Dividing both counts by 2 gives 3:2.

validationMethods: Independent fraction audit: 6/4 = 1.5 and only choice B has first-to-second quotient 1.5 in simplest form.

problem.title: Scale the Packet Batch
problem.statement: For every 5 green packets in a shipment there are 8 yellow packets. If there are 20 green packets, how many yellow packets are there?
hints: Find how many batches of 5 make 20.

solutionSteps.title: Find and apply the scale
solutionSteps.body: 20 ÷ 5 = 4 batches. Scale 8 yellow packets by the same factor: 8 × 4 = 32.

validationMethods: Batch count: 20/5 = 4 and four groups of 8 total 32.
Independent proportion audit: 5/8 = 20/x gives 5x = 160 and x = 32; only C matches.
notes: The context differs from the teaching anchor while preserving near transfer.

problem.title: Find the Equivalent Ratio
problem.statement: Which ratio is equivalent to 12:18 and written in simplest whole-number form?
hints: Divide both entries by their greatest common factor.

solutionSteps.title: Remove the common scale
solutionSteps.body: Both 12 and 18 are divisible by 6. Dividing both by 6 gives 2:3.

validationMethods: Independent quotient and simplicity audit: 12/18 = 2/3; B alone equals this value and has relatively prime entries.
notes: Choice D is equivalent but deliberately not simplest, as the prompt specifies.

problem.title: Scale a Recipe
problem.statement: A recipe uses 3 cups of flour for every 2 loaves. At the same ratio, how many cups of flour are needed for 8 loaves?

solutionSteps.title: Scale the whole batch
solutionSteps.body: Eight loaves are 4 batches of 2. Four batches use 4 × 3 = 12 cups of flour.

validationMethods: Independent unit-ratio check: 3/2 cups per loaf times 8 loaves equals 12 cups; only D matches.
notes: Units stay paired with corresponding quantities.

problem.title: Complete a Two-Stage Scale
problem.statement: The ratio of square tiles to triangular tiles is 7:9. A design with the same ratio has 36 triangular tiles. How many square tiles does it have?
hints: Keep triangular tiles in the second position and find the factor from 9 to 36.

solutionSteps.title: Follow corresponding positions
solutionSteps.body: The triangular count scales from 9 to 36 by a factor of 4. Scale the square count by 4 as well: 7 × 4 = 28.

validationMethods: Independent cross-product audit: x/36 = 7/9 implies 9x = 252 and x = 28; only C satisfies the ordered ratio.
notes: The challenge stresses correspondence rather than larger arithmetic.
